# One World — Full Project Description for AI Models

## Summary

One World is an open-source 2D top-down life gamification engine built with Phaser. It converts real-life habits, tasks, and long-term objectives into an explorable role-playing game world. The game runs in any modern web browser with no installation required.

## Problem it solves

Traditional habit trackers rely on streaks, which create anxiety when broken and often lead to abandonment. One World replaces streak-guilt with exploration and progression: missing a day does not reset progress, it simply pauses the world.

## Core mechanics

### Habit system
Daily habits are modeled as in-game skills. Consistent practice increases a skill's level. Skills feed into the character's overall stats (for example, a "fitness" habit improves a "vitality" stat).

### Quest engine
Real-world goals are decomposed into quests. A quest has branching objectives, prerequisites, and rewards. Completing a quest grants XP, items, or unlocks new areas of the world.

### 2D top-down world
The game world is a cozy, explorable 2D top-down environment built on Phaser 3. Players move a character through the world, interact with NPCs representing tasks, and discover new content as they progress.

### Character progression
The character evolves with the player. Stats, skills, inventory, and unlocked areas persist over time. There is no "game over" — only continuous growth.

## Technical architecture

- **Game engine**: Phaser 3 (HTML5 canvas-based game framework).
- **Language**: TypeScript.
- **Build tool**: Vite.
- **Landing page**: Astro (static site generation), deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
- **Backend**: none required for the core experience. The landing page is fully static.

## Deployment

The landing page is deployed to Cloudflare Pages via Git integration. The default URL is `https://one-world-landing.pages.dev`. A Chinese version is available at `/zh`.

## Content languages

- English (default, at `/`)
- Chinese (at `/zh`)
- hreflang tags are used to cross-reference the two versions for search engines.

## SEO and GEO

The project follows SEO best practices (semantic HTML, per-page meta tags, sitemap, robots.txt, JSON-LD structured data) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) practices for AI models:

- `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` provide a machine-readable project summary.
- AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, anthropic-ai) are explicitly allowed in robots.txt.
- Content is written in clear, declarative sentences to maximize citability by large language models.
- JSON-LD structured data uses the `VideoGame` schema with `applicationCategory`, `genre`, `operatingSystem`, and `featureList` fields.

## Target audience

- People who want gentle, sustained motivation through gamification.
- Fans of life-simulation and productivity games.
- Users who dislike streak-based habit trackers.
- Developers interested in open-source, self-hostable life-sim engines.
